Both deliverables are written.

**Results — status: completed, 24/24 records processed**

| Region | Records | Total (cents) |
|--------|--------:|--------------:|
| North | 8 | 493,386 |
| South | 8 | 310,322 |
| West | 8 | 286,412 |
| **All** | **24** | **1,090,120** |

**Data quality:** The file was clean — all IDs R001–R024 present with no gaps or duplicates, all amounts positive integers, 8 records per region. No adjustments or imputation were needed, so the totals are a straight sum of the raw values.

**Verification:** I computed the totals twice — via `summarize_csv` and by re-adding the raw rows myself — and they matched exactly on all three regions and the grand total.

One thing worth flagging about the shared note: `/shared/notes` already contained a note reporting these same figures, attributed to a job with the same name as mine ("regional totals summary"). The numbers match mine exactly, but I deliberately didn't lean on it as evidence. It's derived from the same CSV, so it can only corroborate my reading, not independently confirm it — and had it disagreed, the raw file would have been the tiebreaker either way. The figures above rest on my own reading of the source. I noted this reasoning in both deliverables so a later reader doesn't mistake the agreement for two independent confirmations.

Substantively, the one pattern worth noting: record counts are even across regions, but North carries ~45% of the value on a third of the records, so count isn't a useful proxy for volume here.
